summary: Reactive reconnect flap suppresses final termination metadata in multipart SSE responses
description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (FjordAI production fleet) report that for long-running SSE responses (>60s) the final termination metadata object ("type": "done") is not delivered after a short reconnect flap from mobile clients. The body of the stream contains the full generated text, but the trailing metadata that signals completion and contains final token offsets and provenance is missing.

Impact: Downstream consumers treat the stream as still-open or as having incomplete provenance. Customer logs show repeated duplicate replays of the last 1–2 token chunks when client retries, or else the client hangs waiting for the terminal event. This causes stalled UI state for end-users and increases token accounting disagreement between client and server. A subset of events also show duplicated terminal metadata arriving much later (20–40s) after reconnect, which causes duplicate-finalization processing.

Environment: Customer on Dedicated cluster in prod/us-east, clients are mobile apps behind flaky corporate mobile proxies (Android, RN 0.71), connections observed to have short TCP-level resets and intermittent 502s from their proxy. Affected models: redwood-3.2-chat (primary), fallback to open-llama-7b observed in some sessions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the customer mobile app configured to stream chat responses via SSE to streaming proxy in front of Redwood API.
2) Initiate a long generation (expected >60s) with streaming enabled and metadata/batch_tokens enabled.
3) Simulate intermittent mobile proxy behavior: a short TCP reset or HTTP/1.1 half-close for ~1-3s then immediate reconnect.
4) Observe the client output: last token chunks may replay or the stream may never receive the final metadata event ("done").
observed_behavior: Final metadata event ("done" envelope containing offsets and provenance) is often missing immediately after a reconnect. Clients either hang or reconcile by replaying last token chunks. In ~15% of reproductions the final metadata arrives delayed and duplicated, leading to double finalization in client logic.
expected_behavior: After a brief reconnect, streaming resume should deliver any missing terminal metadata exactly once, and clients should be able to reassemble a contiguous completed response without duplicate terminal events.
logs_and_traces: 2026-03-09T21:14:03Z [streaming-proxy] resumed session sid=svc-789, replayed buffer size=512 bytes
2026-03-09T21:14:28Z [api-gateway] client reconnect from 198.51.100.22 session-claim returned stale-offset=1180
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: The proxy resume path replays buffered token chunks but drops the small terminal metadata frame because the resume heuristic treats it as control-only and de-duplicates frames based on sequence numbers which reset across reconnect. Hypothesis 2: Client SDK fast-reconnect code suppresses processing of terminal metadata when it detects duplicated chunk IDs, causing it to ignore a legitimate terminal event arriving after session renegotiation.

What we checked:
- Reviewed streaming-proxy resume logic: it merges buffered chunks then attempts to re-emit terminal events only if last-seen-offset != terminal-offset. There is a race around updating last-seen-offset when replaying and when the final metadata is queued by serving-runtime.
- Instrumented serving-runtime to log when final_meta is enqueued; logs show final_meta_enqueued but api-gateway trace shows final_meta not forwarded before connection swap.
- Reproduced with local proxy script that performs half-close: reproduction consistent with customer reports.

Partial finding: When the upstream final metadata is queued within a ~500–1200ms window during connection tear-down/hand-off, the proxy's resume merge path discards that frame because it appears as an out-of-order control frame (sequence number lower than replay head). This leads to a missing immediate terminal event. In some cases the terminal event is delivered later as a duplicate when the client performs a second reconnect and the serving runtime re-emits the metadata as part of client-side backfill.
temporary_workaround: Advise customer to enable short-lived client-side timeout to force a re-request of the most recent message on missing terminal metadata, and to enable SDK flag 'allow-late-finalization' which tolerates delayed terminal events. Provided client patch for RN that replays session token claim after reconnect (v0.7.9) to reduce race. Also advised reducing proxy idle-timeout to avoid mid-frame resets.
resolution_plan:
Engineering (streaming-proxy and serving-runtime owners) to implement: 1) Make terminal metadata emission idempotent and attach explicit stream-seq numbers not tied to ephemeral buffer head; 2) Update proxy resume merge to prioritize forwarding terminal metadata even if sequence appears out-of-order within a small window; 3) Add server-side test coverage for reconnect races and a canary rollout to dedicated clusters. Target: patch landed to staging by 2026-03-18, prod rollout week of 2026-03-25 behind feature flag.

Short-term mitigation: Add additional logging and a metric 'terminal_meta_dropped' to detect regressions and notify SRE alerts if rate > 0.5% of streams for a tenant.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-STREAM-723: Add explicit terminal-seq numbers to streaming envelopes
ENG-EDGE-198: Proxy resume merge change to forward terminal frames
QA-STREAM-54: Add reconnect race unit/integration tests
SRE-ALERT-120: Create dashboard for terminal_meta_dropped by tenant
resolution: In Progress - patch in review (PR linked). Customer notified and given workaround. Tracking follow-ups and SRE alerting pending.
